description: Run Summary page — the primary post-run analysis view where users understand what happened during a workflow run. Combines AI-generated summaries, status banners, token usage, failure details, and tabbed deep-dive sections (Timeline, Verification, Knowledge, Context, Canvas, Diffs & Replay, Phase Timeline, Feedback Scores, LLM Costs, Errors).

groups.name: Run Outcome at a Glance
groups.description: When a user navigates to the Summary page after a workflow completes, they need to immediately understand the outcome. The page should communicate whether the run succeeded, failed, or was stopped, along with the AI-generated narrative of what was accomplished. This is the most critical information on the page because it determines whether the user needs to take further action or can move on to another task.

assertions.description: The user can immediately determine the overall run status (complete, failed, or stopped) from a prominent status indicator displayed near the top of the page, without needing to scroll or click into sub-sections
The user can read an AI-generated narrative summary that explains what was accomplished during the run, providing a human-readable description of the work done rather than just raw status codes
The user can see whether the stated goal of the workflow was achieved or not, displayed as a clear indicator so they know if follow-up work is needed
The user can see how long the run took, including start and end times, so they can assess execution performance and plan future workflow scheduling

groups.name: Failure Analysis and Recovery
groups.description: When a workflow run fails, users need to understand what went wrong and have options for recovery. The Summary page should prominently display failure details for failed runs and offer a way to continue the run with additional iterations. This is essential for iterative development workflows where partial progress is common and users want to pick up where they left off rather than starting over.

assertions.description: When a run has failed, the user sees a dedicated failure section that explains the error, its cause, and the phase where the failure occurred, so they can diagnose the problem without digging through logs
For finished runs (complete, failed, or stopped), the user can continue the run by specifying additional sessions, allowing iterative progress without losing context from previous iterations
The user can view token usage and cost information for the run, helping them understand resource consumption and optimize future workflow configurations

groups.name: Tabbed Deep-Dive Sections
groups.description: Beyond the top-level summary, users need to drill into specific aspects of the run. The tabbed interface provides organized access to the execution timeline, verification results, knowledge entries, context variables, canvas artifacts, and error monitoring. Each tab serves a distinct analytical purpose, and users should be able to switch between them fluidly to build a complete picture of what happened.

assertions.description: The user can switch to the Timeline tab to see a step-by-step execution history grouped by workflow phase (setup, verification, agentic, completion), giving them a chronological understanding of the run's progression

The user can switch to the Verification tab to review the verification plan and its results, understanding which checks passed, which failed, and how verification outcomes influenced the workflow loop
The user can switch to the Knowledge tab to see findings and knowledge entries that were generated during execution, helping them capture lessons learned and improve future workflows
The user can switch to the Context tab to inspect variables, retry history, and other contextual data that was available during execution, aiding in debugging and workflow refinement
The user can switch to the Canvas tab to view visual artifacts and canvas-based recap data generated during the run, providing a spatial or visual representation of execution results

The user can switch to the Phase Timeline tab to see structured per-phase execution results — one card per workflow phase (setup, verification, agentic, completion) with iteration number, stage index, duration, success badge, step-level breakdown, and commit hash. The tab reflects rows the loop controller persists to runner.phase_results after each phase completes, and updates in real time via the Tauri 'phase-result' event.

groups.name: Phase Timeline Tab — Content & Structure
groups.description: When the Phase Timeline tab is active, the user sees one collapsible card per PhaseResult row. Each card shows the phase name (Setup / Verification / Agentic / Completion), optional iteration number, optional stage index, a success/failure badge, the phase duration, step count (successful/total), and an optional abbreviated 8-char commit hash. Iteration separators appear between cards whenever the iteration field changes, so multi-iteration runs read chronologically. The tab is backed by the get_phase_results Tauri command reading from the runner.phase_results PG table (plan: restate-port-part-a-compensation-and-phase-results.md §2.5).

assertions.description: For each row in runner.phase_results keyed by the current task_run_id, the Phase Timeline tab renders exactly one collapsible card. If get_phase_results returns K rows, the user sees K phase cards.
assertions.precondition: Phase Timeline tab is active and at least one phase_result row exists for the selected run

assertions.description: Every phase card header displays: phase name (capitalized — Setup / Verification / Agentic / Completion), a success/failure badge ('Success' in green or 'Failed' in red), and the phase duration formatted as ms / s / m. When present on the row, the header also shows: stage index ('Stage N'), step count ('X/Y steps' where X is successes and Y is total), and abbreviated 8-char commit hash.
assertions.precondition: Phase Timeline tab is active with at least one card visible

assertions.description: An 'Iteration N' separator header appears between phase cards whenever the iteration field changes from one card to the next (or transitions from null to a number). Multi-iteration runs therefore read as a sequence of iteration sections rather than an undifferentiated list.
assertions.precondition: Phase Timeline tab is active and the selected run has multiple iterations

assertions.description: Clicking a phase card toggles an expansion that reveals the step-level breakdown: one row per StepResultRecord with step_index (#N), step_name (falling back to step_type when absent), step_type label, a success/failure icon, error text (when non-null), and duration. Cards with zero step_results AND no failure_context render without an expand chevron — there's nothing to reveal.
assertions.precondition: Phase Timeline tab is active with at least one card that has step_results

assertions.description: When a card's success is false and failure_context is non-null, expanding the card reveals a red-bordered block labeled 'Failure Context' containing the failure_context text in monospace. This surfaces the first failed step's error message (or the AgenticOutcome error / BudgetExceeded reason) so users diagnose what went wrong without navigating to the Errors tab.
assertions.precondition: Phase Timeline tab is active and at least one failed phase has populated failure_context

assertions.description: When get_phase_results returns an empty array (pre-Phase-2 legacy run, or a run that hasn't started yet, or a run whose phase_results rows were written under a different execution_id), the tab renders 'No phase results yet for this run.' with a subtitle explaining that setup, verification, agentic, and completion phases will appear as they run. No cards render.
assertions.precondition: Phase Timeline tab is active for a run with zero phase_result rows

criteria.textContent: No phase results yet for this run

groups.name: Phase Timeline — PhaseResult Data Correctness
groups.description: The Phase Timeline is a window into the loop controller's structured PhaseResult output. The controller builds one PhaseResult after each phase executor returns (setup, verification, agentic, completion) at four insertion points in loop_controller.rs and loop_handlers.rs, persists it via save_phase_result, and emits it on the Tauri 'phase-result' event. Persistence and emit both key on get_parent_task_id(&config.execution_id) so composed-run children surface under their parent task_run. Correctness assertions describe what the persisted data must look like on the page — deviations indicate bugs in the loop controller's mapping logic, not the UI.

assertions.description: Every card's phase name (after UI capitalization) must be exactly one of: Setup, Verification, Agentic, Completion. Any other label indicates the loop controller wrote an unexpected phase string to runner.phase_results.phase — the column accepts arbitrary text but only those four values are legitimate.
assertions.precondition: Phase Timeline tab is active with at least one card

assertions.description: Setup and Completion cards must NOT appear under an 'Iteration N' separator — their iteration field is null because those phases run once per stage, not per iteration. Verification and Agentic cards MUST appear under an iteration separator. If Setup appears under an iteration or Verification appears without one, the loop controller's iteration mapping at the insertion point is wrong.
assertions.precondition: Phase Timeline tab is active with at least one Setup/Completion card AND at least one Verification/Agentic card

assertions.description: Agentic phase cards must render at least one step row in their step breakdown — the loop controller populates step_results from ctx.dynamic_steps / new_injected_steps specifically so Agentic cards are never blank (plan §2.2 UX note). An empty Agentic card is a regression against the existing Diffs & Replay view. Only legitimate exception: AgenticOutcome::Skipped (no agentic steps defined for the stage), in which case the card may be empty but still exists.
assertions.precondition: Phase Timeline tab is active with at least one Agentic card whose phase actually ran

assertions.description: The 'X/Y steps' label in each card header must match the step rows shown on expansion. X equals the count of step_results with success=true, Y equals total step_results length. If the header shows '3/5' but only 4 step rows render on expansion, a step was lost between the DB row's step_results JSONB and the rendered list — indicates a serialization or React rendering bug.
assertions.precondition: Phase Timeline tab is active with at least one card that has steps > 0 and is expanded

assertions.description: While a workflow is running, new PhaseResult cards should appear in the tab within ~1 second of the loop controller emitting the Tauri 'phase-result' event — the tab's useEffect listens to that event and invalidates the ['phase-results', taskRunId] react-query cache. Users should not need a manual refresh to see the latest phase. If new phases don't appear live, either the loop controller failed to emit, the listener is not attached, or the query key doesn't match.
assertions.precondition: A workflow is currently executing and the Phase Timeline tab is active for that run

assertions.description: For composed-run child workflows (IDs like composed-run-{ts}-workflow-{n}), the loop controller persists phase_results rows under the parent task_run_id via get_parent_task_id remapping — matching the same remap applied by store_verification_phase_result. The tab must show the parent's phase cards (aggregating all children) when the user opens the recap for the parent. If the parent's Phase Timeline is empty despite children running, either the loop controller skipped the remap on write, or RunRecapTab.tsx is querying with the child id instead of parent.
assertions.precondition: A composed-run parent task is selected in the run list

groups.name: Empty and Loading States
groups.description: The Summary page must gracefully handle states where data is not yet available. When a run is loading, the user should see clear progress indication. When no run is selected or no recap data exists, the page should guide the user toward selecting a run or initiating one. These states prevent confusion and ensure the user always knows what to do next.

assertions.description: While recap data is being fetched, the user sees a clear loading indicator that confirms data retrieval is in progress, preventing them from thinking the page is broken
When no recap data is available (no run selected or run has no data), the user sees a helpful message guiding them to select a run or execute a task first, rather than showing a blank page
When recap data fails to load, the user sees a clear error message explaining what went wrong, allowing them to understand the issue and potentially retry

groups.name: Verification Results Pagination
groups.description: The Verification tab paginates iteration results (20 per page) to handle runs with many verification iterations. The latest visible iteration is auto-expanded. A 'Show more' button loads additional iterations.

assertions.description: When more than 20 verification iterations exist, a 'Show more' button appears at the bottom of the iterations list showing the remaining count. Clicking loads the next 20 iterations.
assertions.precondition: A task run with >20 verification iterations is selected and Verification tab is active

assertions.description: The last visible verification iteration is automatically expanded to show its step results, so users immediately see the most recent verification outcome without clicking.
assertions.precondition: At least one verification iteration exists

assertions.description: The TaskRunLivePanel output preview uses virtualized line rendering (react-window) to handle large output. Lines are split and rendered individually, capped at 128px height. A 'Load more' button fetches additional output from the backend.
assertions.precondition: A task run with output is visible in the panel

states.name: Loading — Fetching Recap Data
states.description: Recap data is being fetched. The page shows a pulsing activity icon and 'Loading recap...' text. No run content or tabs are visible.

transitions.name: No recap data available for the selected run

states.name: Error — Failed to Load Recap
states.description: An error occurred while fetching recap data. The page shows a red X icon, 'Failed to load recap' heading, and the error message.

states.name: No Data — No Run Selected or No Recap
states.description: No recap data is available. The page shows a guidance message prompting the user to select a run or execute a task first.

transitions.name: User selects a run from the sidebar

states.name: Run Loaded — Summary and Tabs Visible
states.description: Recap data has loaded. The page displays the compact status strip, AI summary, run details sidebar, and the tabbed content area. The Timeline tab is active by default. Failure section appears when the run has failed.

transitions.name: User selects a different run, triggering a reload

states.name: Tab — Timeline Active
states.description: The Timeline tab is selected, showing staged or step-by-step execution history grouped by workflow phase.

states.name: Tab — Verification Active
states.description: The Verification tab is selected, showing the verification plan and iteration results with pass/fail details.

states.name: Tab — Knowledge Active
states.description: The Knowledge tab is selected, showing findings and knowledge entries generated during execution.

states.name: Tab — Context Active
states.description: The Context tab is selected, showing variables, retry history, and contextual data from execution.

states.name: Tab — Canvas Active
states.description: The Canvas tab is selected, showing visual artifacts and canvas-based recap data.

states.name: Tab — Diffs & Replay Active
states.description: The Diffs & Replay tab is selected, showing durable execution diffs and replay controls.

states.name: Tab — Feedback Scores Active
states.description: The Feedback Scores tab is selected, showing feedback scoring panel for the run.

states.name: Tab — LLM Costs Active
states.description: The LLM Costs tab is selected, showing cost breakdown for the run.

states.name: Tab — Errors Active
states.description: The Errors tab is selected, showing the error monitor with categorized errors and severity badges.

states.name: Tab — Phase Timeline Active
states.description: The Phase Timeline tab is selected, showing structured per-phase execution results as collapsible cards grouped by iteration. Cards cover Setup, Verification, Agentic, and Completion phases with step-level breakdowns, duration, success badges, and commit hashes. Empty state appears for runs with no phase_result rows.
